rationale: mpeg2dec is a decode-loop-dominated media benchmark (~49KB text, 58 functions) whose hottest code (IDCT, VLC/bitstream parsing in getvlc/getbits, motion compensation in recon/motion/form_component_predictio, and the large Decode_Picture control flow) is runtime-sensitive, so the weight table favors cheap, correct, structurally diversifying passes and throttles the expensive ones: SUB and SPLIT get the highest weights because instruction substitution and basic-block splitting add strong static-analysis resistance with near-zero runtime/size cost and minimal correctness risk, making them safe to apply broadly including hot loops; IBR and ICALL get solid but moderated weights since indirect branching and indirect calls defeat static call-graph/CFG recovery well but add dispatch overhead, so the selector should favor applying them to cold/medium functions (gethdr, display, systems, verify, store) rather than the per-pixel loops; IGV is kept moderate because this program is global-table-heavy (quantization matrices, VLC tables, frame buffers in global.h), so global indirection meaningfully hampers data-structure reverse engineering at modest cost; BCF and FLA are weighted lowest, especially on RuntimeCost (0.3/0.25) and SizeCost, because bogus control flow inflates the already-large Decode_Picture/Make_Spatial_Prediction_ bodies and flattening serializes the branch-intensive VLC decode and prediction loops where decoder throughput lives — the selector should restrict them to large cold functions like extension_and_user_data and main's setup paths, preserving correctness (all passes keep CorrectnessRisk at 0.6+ tolerance, with the risk-free SUB/SPLIT near 0.9-0.95) while still layering five distinct obfuscation dimensions for diversity.
